title: Motifs et théorie de Hodge : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (cf. heading: topological base fields R, C). Let K be a topological field isomorphic to C, with no isomorphism chosen; there are exactly two continuous ones, differing by complex conjugation. K canonically contains R as the fixed field of its unique nontrivial continuous automorphism, so K has a canonical conjugation but no preferred square root of -1.

Betti realization. For X smooth projective over K, X(K) is a compact K-analytic manifold. Its singular cohomology H^*(X(K),Q) defines a Betti fibre functor M -> Betti(M) on motives over K. No orientation and no choice of i is needed for this.

Comparison. Betti(M) (x)_Q K is canonically H^*(X(K),K). The analytic (holomorphic) Poincare lemma together with GAGA gives a canonical isomorphism with algebraic de Rham cohomology. Hence there is a canonical tensor isomorphism Betti(M)_K = DR(M).

Real structure and Hodge splitting. This puts on the K-vector space DR(M) a real structure, with real subspace Betti(M)_R; let sigma be the corresponding antilinear involution. The Hodge filtration F on DR(M), together with sigma, gives a unique splitting H^{p,q} = F^p ∩ sigma(F^q). This is a bigrading compatible with total degree (p+q = n on degree n) from which F is recovered via the first index.

Point being prepared. The page breaks off as he begins to say that choosing an isomorphism K -> C transports a complex structure. The next page explains that the Hodge structure in the usual sense, e.g. the Weil operator i^{p-q}, depends on the choice of i, while the bigrading itself is intrinsic. It then treats motives over R: there are two real structures on DR(M_K), sigma (Betti) and tau (descent from R). They commute, and their product is the action of complex conjugation on X(K), i.e. the real Frobenius F_infinity.

Purpose. To set up the archimedean realizations (Betti, de Rham, Hodge) of motives over R and C intrinsically, as fibre functors and extra structures in the Tannakian / motivic Galois group programme.
errors: No real error. The splitting H^{p,q} = F^p ∩ sigma F^q requires F to be n-opposite to its conjugate in each degree n (purity). This holds for H^n of smooth projective varieties but is only implicit for general motives with Tate twists, where p+q equals the weight rather than the cohomological degree.
Minor: 'compatible avec le degré total' should be read as weight = degree for effective pure motives of the form H^n(X).

ideas.what: Working over an abstract topological field K ≅ C without choosing the isomorphism; canonical R ⊂ K and canonical conjugation, but no canonical i
ideas.modern_name: choice-free archimedean realization; the role of choosing sqrt(-1) / 2πi orientation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (care about choices of i in Hodge II, 1971, and Hodge cycles on abelian varieties, 1982)

ideas.what: Betti realization as a fibre functor on motives, with canonical tensor comparison isomorphism Betti(M)_K ≅ DR(M)
ideas.modern_name: Betti-de Rham comparison isomorphism; realization functors of motives
ideas.where_published: Circulated in Grothendieck's motives programme (Demazure's 1969 Bourbaki talk, Saavedra Rivano's 1972 thesis); not in a text by Grothendieck himself

ideas.what: Hodge decomposition recovered from the Hodge filtration and the Betti real structure: H^{p,q} = F^p ∩ conj(F^q)
ideas.modern_name: pure Hodge structure as an opposed filtration

ideas.what: (next page) Motives over R: two commuting real structures on de Rham cohomology whose product is the real Frobenius F_infinity
ideas.modern_name: real Hodge structures with F_infinity; Hodge realization of motives over R
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre (Facteurs locaux des fonctions zêta, 1969/70), Deligne (Valeurs de fonctions L et périodes d'intégrales, 1979)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful, standard set-up of the Betti-de Rham comparison and the Hodge decomposition over an abstract field K ≅ C without choosing i. These are well known: the opposed-filtration viewpoint is in Deligne's Hodge II, and the F_infinity material on the next page is in Serre and Deligne. The insistence on not choosing an isomorphism with C is typical Grothendieck style. It is historically interesting as early bookkeeping that Deligne later formalized, but there is nothing new for a specialist.
